description_full: DLocal Limited, together with its subsidiaries, provides payment processing services worldwide. The company offers a robust pay-in solution to help global merchants expand their online presence and receive payments, including international and local cards, online bank transfers, direct debit, cash, and hundreds of alternative payment methods (APMs). It also provides pay-in solutions for cross-border and local-to-local transactions, as well as pay-out solutions. In addition, the company offers dLocal for Platforms to manage global platform payments. It serves its products to commerce, streaming, ride-hailing, financial services, remittances, advertising, SaaS, travel, e-learning, on-demand delivery, gaming, and crypto industries. The company was founded in 2016 and is headquartered in Montevideo, Uruguay.

financial_summary: DLocal Limited is a mid-cap technology business with a $4.0B market cap on $1.1B of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +38% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder. Operating margins are contracting by -3.6pp, the first warning that competitive pressure is eroding the franchise.
Returns on capital run at 108% against a 11% cost of capital — a 97-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat, with gross margins sitting at 43%.

The business throws off $413M in free cash flow — roughly 38 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 2.11× so those profits are backed by real cash.
Accruals are elevated at -14.2% of assets, and Sloan showed firms building earnings through accruals rather than cash systematically underperform.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage runs at 7.9×.

Shareholder yield of 2.5% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insiders hold 23% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is.

sect: Its 20% operating margin runs 13pp above the Technology median (7%), a real cost or pricing edge over peers.

mkt: The shares have drifted higher, up 9% over the past year excluding the latest month, though it has pulled back 9% over the last three months.
The price sits mid-way through its 52-week range, 14% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 44% and a beta of 1.28, it amplifies market moves, though its beta has shifted (1y 1.17 vs 5y 1.68), so read it loosely.

The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 55%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $20.61 to $60.49 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.
On multiples it looks cheap against Technology peers: P/E 20.5 vs 26.7, EV/EBITDA 12.9 vs 16.4 and P/FCF 9.7 vs 25.4 (sector median).

Earnings yields are mixed: an FCF yield of 10.3% (above the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 7.0% (vs the 8% bar).
The 10 covering analysts target $18.60 on average, 33% above the price, well away from the model's fair value.
prof: ROIC of 108% clears the cost of capital of 11.1% by 97pp, the mark of a value creator.
It runs a 43% gross margin and converts 38% of revenue into free cash flow.
Earnings quality is mixed: cash conversion of 2.11x, but high accruals (-14.2% of assets).
ROE of 35% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (2.7x equity multiplier).
hlth: The balance sheet carries net cash of $633.2M.
No distress or manipulation flags (Altman Z 4.5, in the safe zone).
growth: Revenue has compounded at 37.7% over 3 years, and it has been lumpy (year-to-year swings of 21%).
At current returns, reinvesting 19% of profits supports about 20.4% a year of fundamental growth, enough to sustain growth.
It has beaten earnings estimates by 10.0% on average.
Analysts expect 34.0% long-term annual earnings growth.
own: Insiders own 23.2%, meaningful skin in the game, and institutions hold 71%.
Insider trading is two-way: 1 purchase and 4 sales over the past year, net $16.0M sold.
It returns 2.5% a year to shareholders (1.4% in dividends, less 1.3% of net share issuance).
Short interest is elevated at 14.2% of the float, 10.2 days to cover.
people: With about 1,274 employees, each generates about $858K of revenue, 2.3x the Technology median, and productivity has risen 45.5% a year.
That works out to $324K of free cash flow per employee.
